title: Thursday, 4:12 P.M.
subtitle: The Afternoon the Bridges Went Up

setting.name: The Meridian: Union Terminal to the Forty-First Street Library
setting.description: Six blocks of midtown Merriwick on the first afternoon and night of the Arrival. Union Terminal sits at the centre: a Beaux-Arts concourse the size of a cathedral, with a painted ceiling of green-and-gold constellations, a four-faced brass clock over the information booth, and nine subway lines and two commuter railroads underneath. Outside on Kestrel Avenue, a hundred and forty stopped cars, Benny Szabo's double-decker tour bus at the kerb, and a sky that is the wrong colour. Two blocks west on Forty-First Street, Osteria Sette, where Hector Salgado was prepping a hundred and ten covers. Between them, a pharmacy, a parking garage, a church and a long, glass-fronted avenue of office lobbies. And at Forty-First and Bramwell, guarded by two enormous stone owls, the Merriwick Public Library — a granite fortress of reading rooms with thick walls, few windows at street level and, by midnight, forty-one frightened people in it. All six player characters are within three hundred yards of the Terminal clock at 4:12. By midnight they will have found each other, and they will know one rule.
setting.atmosphere: The first hour is a stampede and then a silence. The thing to get right is the turn from chaos to eeriness: at 4:12 there are screams, a crush at the Terminal doors, cars abandoned with their engines running; by 6:00 the Meridian has emptied to a few people walking very carefully, and the traffic lights are still changing for nobody. The Visitors are not hurrying and they are not angry. A Stilt comes down Kestrel Avenue at walking pace like a fourteen-foot heron made of lacquered glass, bending to examine a car alarm, a dropped phone that is ringing, a man who is running — and it walks straight past a woman in a business suit walking calmly to the subway with her coffee. The players should leave this scenario frightened, oddly moved, and in possession of a hypothesis.

keyLocations.name: Union Terminal Concourse
keyLocations.description: The great hall: 275 ft long, 125 ft high, marble floor, painted sky-ceiling, the four-faced brass clock on the information booth, the departure board, east and west stairs to the street, and ramps down to the subway mezzanine. Four hundred people at 4:12, about thirty by 5:00.
features: The four-faced clock, which stops at 4:12 for exactly one minute and then starts again — four seconds slow, and losing one second an hour all week (the first sign of the Countdown)
The departure board, every tile blank white and humming
The west windows, through which the Kingsgate span is seen lifting away over the rooftops
Ramps down to the subway mezzanine, where the trains have stopped in their stations with their doors open
The east stair, where a busker's saxophone lies on its side, and a hot-dog cart still steaming
encounters: The crush at the west doors at 4:13 (Act 1)
A Glitter swarm drifting down from the ceiling vents into the noise
The first Lifting: a man who runs across the concourse shouting a name
secrets: The Glitter records the concourse's screaming at 4:13 and will play it back in the Library at 2 A.M.
The lower-level Green Line platform is the deepest point in the Meridian, and Attention rises at half rate down there — Lo Pruitt knows it as 'the Cellar'

keyLocations.name: Kestrel Avenue
keyLocations.description: The Meridian's great north-south avenue, eight lanes between glass towers, with the Terminal's façade on one side. At 4:12 every traffic light on the avenue showed a fourth colour — a soft pearly white — for nine seconds, and every car stopped. Most of their drivers got out and ran. Some are still sitting at the wheel.
features: Wick Sightseer bus #14 at the kerb outside the Terminal, engine idling, fourteen tourists on the top deck
A hundred and forty abandoned cars, a dozen with their engines running and three with alarms that will go off if jostled
Traffic lights that went back to normal at 4:12 and nine seconds, and have been changing on their timers ever since
A Set cab driver at the corner of Forty-Second, leaning out of his window, mid-shout, over and over
encounters: The first Stilt walking down the avenue at 4:25
The man on the bicycle beside Teo, Lifted
The car-alarm Lifting on Forty-Third at 4:31 (Calla Moreno's alarm; she is on the fire escape above)
secrets: Bus #14 can be driven in pattern — at the speed limit, in lane, stopping at the lights — which June or Benny may work out by watching the Stilt ignore a Set taxi that is still idling forward through green lights
There is a pistol in the glovebox of a black SUV on the corner of Forty-Third (a 9mm, 9 rounds); finding it is Investigation DC 15, and the SUV's alarm is armed

keyLocations.name: Osteria Sette, Forty-First Street
keyLocations.description: A narrow, deep, old Italian restaurant with a tin ceiling, a long bar, a dining room for sixty and a kitchen out back with a walk-in, a basement and a fire door onto the alley. Hector Salgado's kitchen; his cooks Dee, Kwame and fifteen-year-old Rafi are still in it at 4:30, hiding in the walk-in.
features: Gas burners that went out at 4:12 and relight perfectly well afterwards (the gas is fine; the Visitors did not do anything to the gas)
A walk-in fridge with food for a hundred and ten covers and a thick door
A basement with a second exit into the building next door's boiler room
A wall of knives
encounters: Finding the cooks in the walk-in
A Glitter swarm attracted to the kitchen's fire alarm, if anyone lights a burner with the hood off
secrets: The restaurant's food is the best resource in six blocks, and carrying it to the Library is how the party earns the shelter's trust
Rafi, the dishwasher, films everything on his phone. In the walk-in he has a nine-second video of the Stilt ignoring the woman with the coffee

keyLocations.name: Halvard Pharmacy, Kestrel and Forty-Second
keyLocations.description: A big chain pharmacy with its shutters half down. At 6 P.M. four young men are inside clearing the pharmacy counter, and one of them has a baseball bat and the conviction that the world has ended and the rules with it.
features: The pharmacy counter: insulin, antibiotics, painkillers, inhalers
A half-lowered steel shutter that screams when raised (+2 Attention)
A back stockroom with a door to a service corridor under the street
encounters: The looters (Act 2)
secrets: One of the looters, Andre, is getting insulin for his diabetic little sister at home in the Middle Wards and will stop the moment someone notices which shelf he went for

keyLocations.name: The Merriwick Public Library, Forty-First and Bramwell
keyLocations.description: A granite palace of a library with two stone owls on its steps, a reading room the length of a city block under a coffered ceiling, stacks seven storeys deep under the back lawn, and thick walls. By 9 P.M. forty-one people are sheltering in it, led — loosely — by the night librarian, Margaret 'Peg' Odinga, who refused to go home.
features: The Rose Reading Room, with long oak tables, brass lamps and windows thirty feet up
The stacks: seven levels of iron shelving underground, cool, silent, and very dark when the power fails
A staff kitchen, restrooms, a first-aid room and a loading dock onto the back alley
A roof reachable by a staff stair, from which the Greensward Lantern can be seen at night, glowing in the Reservoir thirty blocks north
encounters: Arriving, and being let in (Act 3)
Gerry Voss and his pistol
The 2 A.M. playback
secrets: The stacks are the safest place in the Meridian: underground, insulated, and the Visitors do not go below the street
Peg Odinga has a hand-crank emergency radio and is the first person to hear the mainland stations

synopsis: The Arrival, and the first night. At 4:12 P.M. on a Thursday the six player characters are within a few hundred yards of each other around Union Terminal in the Meridian when the light changes, every phone sounds one tone, and the river span of the Kingsgate Bridge rises over the rooftops and drifts away north with its traffic still on it. The Terminal stampedes. In the next hour the party will see the first Stilt walk down Kestrel Avenue, see it Lift a running man off the street and walk past a woman walking to the subway, and — if they are watching — begin to understand that the things in the street do not see what the city does every day. They will find each other, collect the people who attach themselves to them (Benny's fourteen tourists, June's three students, Hector's cooks), deal with frightened and armed humans, and reach the Forty-First Street Library by nightfall. The scenario ends at dawn on Day 2 with a working hypothesis, a radio voice from the mainland saying the island is surrounded by something nobody can cross, and the sound of the Pier Point ferry's horn at 6:00 A.M. exactly, carrying three miles up the empty avenues, on schedule.
hook: Every player character is somewhere in or around Union Terminal at 4:12 (see dmTips for each one's opening position). Open on each in turn for one sentence of ordinary Thursday — a coffee, a last drop, a field trip, a tour speech, a hundred and ten covers, a birthday card — and then: “The light changes. Not darker. Different, as if somebody had replaced the sun with a more careful one. Every phone in the city plays the same note, a long low tone that none of them were built to make, and a quarter of a mile east, over the rooftops, the Kingsgate Bridge comes up out of the river haze — the whole river span, lit, with the five o’clock traffic still on it — and turns once, slowly, as if it were being shown to you. Then it drifts north over the towers like a leaf on a pond, and the city is silent for exactly four seconds. You will remember those four seconds for the rest of your life. Then the screaming starts.”

acts.title: Act 1: The Four Seconds
acts.description: 4:12 to about 4:40. The Arrival, the stampede in the Terminal, the first Stilt on Kestrel Avenue, the first Liftings. The party members find each other — or at least see each other — and the players see the rule in action without being told it. Run this fast, in short cuts between characters, and let it be loud; it is the last loud thing in the campaign.
objectives: Survive the crush in the Terminal and get some people out of it alive
See a Stilt Lift someone who is running, and walk past someone who is not
Bring the six player characters together near the Terminal or the bus
Get off Kestrel Avenue before the second Stilt arrives at about 4:40
encounters: The crush at the west doors (skill challenge)
A Glitter swarm on the concourse (optional fight, Easy)
The first Stilt on Kestrel Avenue (evasion, not a fight)

scenes.name: The Crush
scenes.description: Four hundred people on the concourse try to leave through the west doors at once. The doors are pull-to-open. This is a real disaster — crowd crushes kill people — and the characters inside the Terminal (Lo, Abena, June, possibly Teo coming in off the avenue) have about two minutes to make a difference.
scenes.readAloud: “The whole hall moves at once, the way water moves when you pull a plug. Toward the west doors, toward the bridge, toward the light, which makes no sense and which everybody does anyway. Somebody goes down on the marble near the information booth and the crowd closes over the space where they were. The doors are brass and glass and they open inward, and the people at the front are pressed flat against them by the people behind, and you can see faces against the glass, and the clock over the booth has stopped, and over the noise a busker’s saxophone, dropped, is still sliding down the east stair one step at a time.”

skillChecks.success: A voice with authority (Lo's thirty-one years, or anyone who can manage it) turns the back of the crowd toward the east stair and the ramps. The pressure on the west doors eases and nobody dies there.
skillChecks.failure: Nobody hears you. The crush runs its course: 1d4+2 people are seriously injured at the doors, and Abena will have them in front of her in five minutes.

skillChecks.success: You get to the doors from the side and throw the brass bolts on the second set, which open outward. The pressure goes out of the crowd like air from a tyre.
skillChecks.failure: You are carried twenty feet by the crowd and take 1d6 bludgeoning, and you end up on the street outside without having chosen to.

skillChecks.success: You find the woman who went down by the booth, get her airway clear and her on her side, and she lives. Her name is Corinne, she is a paralegal, and she will follow you anywhere.
skillChecks.failure: You reach her, and she is breathing, but you cannot keep her and keep moving. A stranger stays with her. You will not see either again until the Greensward.

skillChecks.success: In the middle of the stampede you notice something nobody else does: the Set. A man at the newsstand is paying for a paper, over and over, smiling. A woman on the east stair is checking her watch, lowering it, checking it again. They are not panicking. They are not anything.
skillChecks.failure: Nothing but bodies and noise.

enemies: 1 Glitter swarm (only if the Attention reaches 2 — which, in a stampede, it does at the start of round 2)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Glitter drifts down from the ceiling vents like glitter in a snow globe, settling over the loudest part of the crowd. It does not attack anyone who leaves it alone. It attacks (Static) only a creature that strikes it, sprays it or screams inside it. The point of the encounter is the image and the lesson: it is listening, and it can hurt you if you hit it. A character who sprays it with a fire extinguisher learns it hates that.
combatEncounters.terrain: A packed marble concourse. Moving through the crowd is difficult terrain until the crush clears. The information booth is half cover. The ramps to the subway are open.
combatEncounters.statblock: GLITTER (Medium swarm of Tiny aberrations, CR 1). AC 12. HP 22 (5d8). Speed 0 ft, fly 30 ft (hover). STR 3 (-4) DEX 15 (+2) CON 10 (+0) INT 1 (-5) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 1 (-5). Resistances bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Immunities grappled, paralyzed, prone, restrained, frightened. Senses blindsight 60 ft. Swarm: it can occupy another creature's space and move through openings an inch wide; it cannot regain HP. Record: the Glitter remembers every sound made within 30 ft of it. It replays them later, elsewhere, at random — a dead man's voice, the party's names, a gunshot — and each replay in a scene is +1 Attention. Harmless in Pattern: a Glitter swarm does not attack anything unless it is struck, sprayed, burned or shouted at from inside it. Actions — Static: every creature in the swarm's space makes a CON save DC 12, 2d6 lightning damage on a failure, half on a success (1d6 if the swarm is at half HP or less). Behaviour: drifts like dust in a sunbeam, towards novelty. It is the Visitors' ears. Fire disperses it (a burning swarm takes double damage), and a fire extinguisher's cone deals it 2d6 cold.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Do not let this become a combat. The crush is the enemy. Reward any player who stops to help rather than run, and quietly note who ran: the Ushers and Stilts will be on the avenue in ten minutes and running is the one thing they see. The Set people on the concourse are the players' first sight of the campaign's central mystery, and nobody explains them.
loot: A fire extinguisher from the concourse wall (June's, if she is the one who grabs it)
Corinne, if she lives: a paralegal with a good memory and a laptop bag

scenes.name: The First Stilt
scenes.description: At about 4:25 a Stilt comes down Kestrel Avenue from the north at walking pace. Characters outside — Teo on his bike, Benny on his bus, Hector in his apron on Forty-First — see it first. It is fourteen feet tall, three-legged, with a long tilted body like a heron's made of dark lacquered glass, and a fan of fine shining filaments that it lowers over things to read them. It is not the most frightening thing about this scene. The frightening thing is what it does and does not do.
scenes.readAloud: “It walks like something that has never been in a hurry. Three long legs, jointed backwards, stepping between the stopped cars with a precision that makes your skin crawl, and above them a long dark body, tilted forward, glossy as a beetle and seamed with light. It stops at a car with its alarm going and lowers a fan of fine threads over the hood — reading it — and the alarm stops. Then a man in a suit, forty feet from you, breaks and runs, shouting something, a name, and the thing turns — not its head, it does not have a head, the whole of it turns — and in two strides it is over him and he is off the ground and gone up into the threads, still shouting, and then not. And then it walks on. It passes within an arm’s length of a woman in a grey coat who is walking very calmly up the avenue toward the subway with a coffee, and it does not slow down. It does not even seem to see her.”

skillChecks.success: You do not run. You keep doing the ordinary thing — walking, sitting at the wheel, standing in your apron — and it walks past you. You have just survived the most important test in the campaign, and you may not know why.
skillChecks.failure: You flinch, you shout, you start to run. You are Out of Pattern for one round (+1 Attention). If the Attention reaches 4, the Stilt turns toward you. An ally can grab you (Athletics DC 10) and walk you out of it.

skillChecks.success: June Halvorsen (or whoever is watching closely) sees the pattern: everyone it has taken was running, shouting or making a noise; everyone walking in a straight line at a normal pace it has passed. Make the player say it out loud. Write it down. It is a hypothesis, not a rule — yet.
skillChecks.failure: You see it take people and leave people and you cannot see why. It looks random. It is not.

skillChecks.success: You get yourself and anyone with you behind something solid — the bus, a lobby door — and out of the street before it comes level with you.
skillChecks.failure: You are still in the open when it comes level. Make a Keep Walking check.

combatEncounters.difficulty: Deadly (do not run this as a fight)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Stilt walks the length of Kestrel Avenue from Forty-Sixth to Thirty-Eighth in about ten minutes, reading every alarm and Lifting every runner. It ignores anything In Pattern. If a character attacks it, it Lifts that character — Lift damage applies, and a Lifted PC is carried toward the Greensward and must escape the grapple (DC 15) or be rescued within two rounds. If the party somehow brings it below 20 HP, it folds and sounds its falling tone and the Attention goes to 6 for the whole Meridian: the second Stilt and four Ushers arrive in 1d4 rounds. A level 1 party that fights this should be in serious trouble in two rounds. Let them.
combatEncounters.terrain: Eight lanes of stopped cars (half cover against everything; engine blocks are full cover), office lobbies with glass doors (the Stilt cannot fit through), the bus, the Terminal's façade, side streets.
combatEncounters.statblock: STILT (Large aberration, CR 4). AC 15 (lacquered carapace). HP 68 (8d10+24). Speed 30 ft, climb 20 ft. STR 18 (+4) DEX 12 (+1) CON 16 (+3) INT 14 (+2) WIS 16 (+3) CHA 5 (-3). Saves WIS +5. Skills Perception +7. Resistances piercing, bludgeoning. Vulnerabilities thunder. Condition immunities frightened, charmed. Senses tremorsense 120 ft, blindsight 30 ft; it does not see light at all. Pattern-Blind: it cannot perceive a creature that is In Pattern unless the scene's Attention is 6 or that creature has harmed it. Dread: WIS save DC 12 on first sight (campaign rules). No Anatomy: called shots and Precision Strike-style bonus damage from 'vital spots' do not apply; criticals still double dice. Actions — Multiattack: two Lift attempts, or one Hum. Lift: melee +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, one creature: 2d6+4 bludgeoning (it is not trying to hurt you; that is just what its grip does) and the target is grappled (escape DC 15). On its next turn it carries a grappled creature toward the nearest Lantern at full speed; a creature carried out of sight is gone, and returns Set within the hour. Hum (recharge 5-6): a 30-ft cone of resonance; CON save DC 13, 3d8 thunder damage and Shaken on a failure, half damage and not Shaken on a success. Glass in the cone breaks (+1 Attention). Behaviour: a Stilt walks streets slowly, bending to 'read' anything novel with a fan of fine glassy filaments; it Lifts whatever is Out of Pattern and ignores everything else. It does not pursue into buildings narrower than its 10-ft frame, does not go underground, and if reduced below 20 HP it stops, folds, and gives a long falling tone that sets the Attention in the whole district to 6. Killing one is possible. It is almost always a mistake.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scene the campaign is built on. Run the Stilt in complete silence: describe what it does, never what it wants. Do not tell the players about In Pattern; let them see the woman with the coffee and let them argue about it. A player who works it out here gets a real advantage for the rest of the scenario. If Teo is on his bike, the cyclist beside him who keeps pedalling hard and fast is Lifted; Teo, who put a foot down, is not. If Benny is on the bus, the Stilt passes along the bus's whole length at the height of the top deck, its threads drifting over the heads of his fourteen tourists, and if he keeps talking in his ordinary tour voice they keep sitting still, and it moves on. That is a scene the table will remember.
loot: Rafi's nine-second video of the woman with the coffee (if the party meets Hector's cooks)

scenes.name: Forty-Third Street, 4:31
scenes.description: A car alarm goes off on Forty-Third Street, a block north. A Stilt crosses to it, reads the car, and then Lifts the one person on the corner who stopped to look at the noise: a woman in a green raincoat holding her phone up to film. On the fire escape directly above, a girl in a black hoodie is watching with both hands over her mouth. That is Calla Moreno, and she set the alarm off.
scenes.readAloud: “It is the ordinary sound that is worst: a car alarm, whooping, the noise you have heard ten thousand times on this island and never once looked up at. Everybody on Forty-Third looks up at it now. A woman in a green raincoat on the corner stops and lifts her phone to film the car. The tall thing is already crossing to it. It reads the car and the alarm stops, and then the threads drift sideways, onto her, and she goes up into them with her phone still held out in front of her, filming. On the fire escape above the car, a kid in a black hoodie is staring down, both hands over her mouth.”

skillChecks.success: You see the girl on the fire escape, and you see that the sedan's driver-side window is broken from the outside, and that the girl's sleeve is cut. She did it. She will not admit it for days.
skillChecks.failure: Just a kid on a fire escape.

skillChecks.success: Calla Moreno comes down and talks to you, with contempt, and then — because you are the first adults she has seen who are not running — tells you the one thing she has worked out from forty storeys up: 'They don't see you if you're boring.' She will travel with the party, on her terms.
skillChecks.failure: She is gone up the fire escape and over the roofs in about four seconds. She will turn up again at the Library at midnight, having followed the party the whole way, and act as if it was her idea.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Introduce Calla here. She is a companion NPC and she is the party's route-finder. Do not reveal what she did; let the broken window be noticed or not. The woman in the green raincoat will be in the Greensward among the Set in lf-scenario-002, still filming.

acts.title: Act 2: Keep Walking
acts.description: About 4:40 to 9:00 P.M. The Meridian empties. The party gathers its people and works out where to go — the obvious answers (the hospital, the bridges, home) are all wrong or impossible tonight — and tests the hypothesis on the way. Scavenging, the looters at the pharmacy, an Usher pair on Bramwell Avenue, and a long, slow, terrifying walk.
objectives: Gather the party's people: Benny's fourteen tourists, June's three students, Hector's three cooks, and whoever else attached themselves in Act 1
Scavenge food, water, light and medicine before the dark
Test the 'boring' hypothesis and survive the test
Reach a defensible shelter before full dark (the Library, the Terminal's lower level, or the restaurant)
encounters: The looters in the Halvard Pharmacy (social or Easy fight)
Two Ushers on Bramwell Avenue (Medium; evasion preferred)
Moving a Group of twenty-plus civilians six blocks in pattern (skill challenge)

scenes.name: What Now
scenes.description: The party regroups at the bus, the restaurant or the Terminal steps. Phones still work for about two hours, badly: news feeds full of the bridges, a mainland emergency broadcast telling Merriwick residents to shelter in place, texts from people who are fine and people who are not answering. Everyone has somewhere they want to be. Lo's grandson is in a school in Harlow, eighty blocks north. Abena's hospital is a mile and a half east. Hector's mother is in Harlow. Benny's fourteen want to go to their hotel, which is on the Tidewater waterfront, which is now a long way from a bridge. Nobody can get anywhere tonight.
scenes.readAloud: “Six o’clock in the Meridian and the streets have emptied the way a beach empties when the tide goes out — all at once, leaving things behind. Shoes. A stroller. Phones face-down on the asphalt, ringing. The traffic lights on Kestrel Avenue are still changing, red to green to amber to red, for a hundred and forty cars with nobody in them. Somewhere a few blocks over a dog is barking and then stops. To the north, over the towers, there is a light in the sky above the Greensward that was not there this morning: a tall soft column, the colour of a paper lantern, very far away and very, very big.”

skillChecks.success: Teo, Calla or Lo knows that the Library on Forty-First has thick walls, a basement seven floors deep, a night librarian who will not leave and a loading dock off a back alley. It is the best building in six blocks.
skillChecks.failure: You can think of a dozen places and every one of them has glass doors.

skillChecks.success: On a dying phone you get one useful thing out of the internet before the network chokes: a mainland news helicopter's live feed of the island from twelve miles away, showing a faint shimmering ring on the water all the way round the shoreline — and a Coast Guard boat approaching it, slowing, turning in a long, gentle arc, and coming back toward the island with its crew standing perfectly still on deck.
skillChecks.failure: Spinning wheels and 'No Service'.

skillChecks.success: You talk the group out of the obvious, fatal plan (somebody always wants to walk to a bridge). They agree to shelter for the night and go in the morning. Each Group gains +1 Calm.
skillChecks.failure: One of Benny's tourists, Mr. Okafor, sets off east with his wife and twins to find a bridge, and Benny will have to choose whether to go after them.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Give each player character a pull in a different direction and do not let any of them resolve tonight. The answer to 'can I go to Harlow/Eastgate now' is 'you can try': it is eighty blocks in the dark through an island full of Stilts. The point is that the party chooses to stay together — and the people with them are why.
loot: Whatever the party grabs from the restaurant: the walk-in holds food for about sixty people for two days

scenes.name: The Halvard Pharmacy
scenes.description: Four young men in the Halvard Pharmacy on Kestrel and Forty-Second, shutters half down, clearing the counter into duffel bags. Abena wants the insulin and antibiotics. One of them, Kenny, has a baseball bat and the conviction that this is the end of the world. One, Andre, is just getting insulin for his sister.
scenes.readAloud: “The shutter on the Halvard Pharmacy is down to waist height and there is light moving inside — phone torches, three or four of them — and the sound of shelves being swept. Somebody inside laughs, high and frightened. A boy of maybe nineteen ducks out under the shutter with a duffel bag in each hand and sees you and stops, and behind him a bigger one comes out with an aluminium bat on his shoulder and says, very loudly, ‘Keep walking, man. Keep walking.’ He has no idea how right he is.”

skillChecks.success: Kenny is the only one who wants a fight. Andre, with the insulin, is terrified; the other two will follow whichever way the room goes.
skillChecks.failure: Four of them, one armed, all of them looking at you.

skillChecks.success: You split them. Andre gives you half of what he took, keeps the insulin, and asks if he can come with you. Kenny walks away swearing — loudly, in the street, which is a very bad idea. Let the party hear what happens to him, a block away, and not see it.
skillChecks.failure: Kenny swings. It is a fight, and it is loud.

skillChecks.success: They leave the bags and go. You have the pharmacy, and four young men who will tell everyone they meet tonight about the crazy people on Forty-Second.
skillChecks.failure: Kenny swings.

skillChecks.success: Abena knows what to take from the shelves without reading labels: insulin, antibiotics, inhalers, epinephrine, a box of the good painkillers. That is a week of medicine for forty people.
skillChecks.failure: Half the pharmacy is on the floor and the labels are in the dark.

enemies: Kenny (Street Thug, with an aluminium bat: 1d6+2 bludgeoning)
2 looters (Civilian; they flee at the first blood)
combatEncounters.tactics: Kenny swings at whoever is closest and shouts the whole time. The other two run on round 2. Each round of fighting in the open is +1 Attention for the noise; the shutter, if anyone raises it fully, is +2. At Attention 4 a Stilt turns down Forty-Second; the fight ends however it ends, and Kenny, who is running and shouting, is the one who is Lifted. The lesson should not be lost on anyone.
combatEncounters.terrain: The pharmacy shop floor: shelving units (half cover vs. a thrown bat, nothing vs. anything else), a counter, broken glass (difficult terrain), the half-lowered shutter.
combatEncounters.statblock: Use LookupMonster 'Street Thug' for Kenny and 'Civilian' for the others.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the first time the party fights a human being, and they are ordinary people; make it ugly and short. Reward talking. Andre, if the party is kind to him, will walk his insulin home to his sister in the Middle Wards at dawn, In Pattern, at commuting pace — and the party should hear him say, 'I'm just going to walk like I'm going to work,' and realise he got the rule from them.
loot: Pharmacy medicine (DC 10: painkillers, bandages, a medkit's worth; DC 15 with Abena: insulin, antibiotics, inhalers, epinephrine — a week for forty people)
Batteries (AA and AAA, 48 of each), flashlights, a hand-crank phone charger
Bottled water (two cases) and as much candy as anyone can carry

scenes.name: Bramwell Avenue: the Ushers
scenes.description: Moving the party's people — call it twenty-five to thirty, in two Groups — the six blocks from Kestrel Avenue to the Library down Bramwell Avenue, at dusk. Halfway, two Ushers come out of the Greensward end of the avenue, low and quick and glinting, quartering the street like sheepdogs. They are looking for movement.
scenes.readAloud: “They come down Bramwell Avenue from the north in long low bounds, and at first you think they are dogs. They are the size of dogs. They are not dogs. Six legs, folded like the legs of a praying mantis, bodies of overlapping glassy plates that catch the last of the light and break it into colours, and they make a sound when they move like a fingertip run around the rim of a wine glass. Two of them. They stop at the end of the block and do not look at anything, and then the one on the left swings its whole body toward a pigeon that has just taken off, and is on it in a single bound, and the pigeon is simply not there any more.”

skillChecks.success: Benny (Performance), Lo (Insight) or whoever leads each Group keeps them walking — not too fast, not too slow, chatting, eyes front, the way people walk home on a Thursday evening. The Ushers flow around the Group like water around a stone and lose interest. Each Group that succeeds is In Pattern; nobody is touched.
skillChecks.failure: Someone in the Group breaks. A child runs, a tourist screams. That Group is Out of Pattern and loses 1 Calm, and an Usher comes for whoever ran. Someone has to make them stop moving — tackle them (Athletics DC 12) and hold still — or the Usher Herds them toward Kestrel Avenue, where the Stilt is.

skillChecks.success: You see the second rule: an Usher that cannot see anything moving stops and circles, like a dog that has lost a scent. Stillness works on them. It does not work on the Stilts.
skillChecks.failure: You see them go for movement. You do not see them stop.

skillChecks.success: June's Analyze on an Usher gives the next ally to act against it advantage — and a player using Analyze may ask the GM one question about how it perceives. Answer truthfully: 'It feels the ground. It feels movement. It does not see you at all.'

combatEncounters.difficulty: Medium (for a level 1 party, a real danger)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Ushers herd rather than kill. Each round, each one goes for the fastest-moving creature it can feel: Herd if it can push them toward Kestrel Avenue, Nip if they resist. They Chime when they lose prey (+1 Attention). They break off and circle if nothing in the street moves more than 10 ft for a full round. Fighting them is possible (33 HP, AC 14, resistant to piercing) and loud; a party that kills one will find the other Chimes until a Stilt answers in 1d4+1 rounds.
combatEncounters.terrain: A wide avenue with parked cars both sides (half cover; Ushers go over and under them), shop doorways (an Usher can follow into a doorway but not through a closed door), a subway entrance (stairs down: the Ushers will not follow below street level), a scaffold walkway over the sidewalk.
combatEncounters.statblock: USHER (Medium aberration, CR 2). AC 14 (folded glass plates). HP 33 (6d8+6). Speed 50 ft. STR 14 (+2) DEX 18 (+4) CON 12 (+1) INT 6 (-2) WIS 14 (+2) CHA 3 (-4). Skills Perception +4, Stealth +6. Resistances piercing. Senses tremorsense 60 ft. Pattern-Blind (as Stilt). Herding: it has advantage on attack rolls and shoves against any creature that moved more than 10 ft on its last turn — running is the thing it hunts. Stillness: an Usher that cannot perceive movement in a creature for a full round (the creature took no move and no action except Keep Walking or Dodge) loses track of it and circles. Actions — Nip: melee +6 to hit, 1d8+4 piercing. Herd: the Usher shoves a creature up to 10 ft in a direction of its choice (contest: its Athletics +2 with advantage from Herding if applicable, against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics); used to push people toward a Stilt or a Lantern. Bonus action — Chime: it rings like a struck glass; every Usher within 300 ft knows where it is (+1 Attention). Behaviour: Ushers come in twos and fours and work like sheepdogs, not wolves. They want to drive runners toward a Stilt to be Lifted. They bite only what resists. They break off when nothing in the scene is moving fast.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the party's first real test of the rule with stakes, and the Groups are the stakes. Make it clear that their people are watching how they behave. If the party freezes, the Ushers sweep past; if they run, it becomes a fight in the open at dusk. The subway entrance is the panic button: anyone who gets down the stairs is safe from the Ushers, which teaches the party about the Under for later.

acts.title: Act 3: The First Night
acts.description: 9 P.M. to dawn, in the Forty-First Street Library. Forty-one strangers, one stone building, the dark, the first broadcast from the mainland, a frightened man with a gun, the Glitter's playback at 2 A.M., and a ferry horn at six. The party becomes the people everyone else in the building looks at.
objectives: Get the party and its people into the Library and accepted by those already there
Keep the shelter quiet and In Pattern through the night
Deal with Gerry Voss and his pistol without a shot being fired
Hear the mainland broadcast, and the ferry horn, and decide what to do on Day 2
encounters: Gerry Voss (social; a single shot is +3 Attention in the building)
The 2 A.M. playback (a Glitter swarm in the reading room; Easy fight or a test of nerve)

scenes.name: Between the Owls
scenes.description: The Library's front doors are bronze and locked. The night librarian, Peg Odinga, sixty, Kenyan-born, unflappable, lets people in through the loading dock in the back alley one at a time and makes each of them tell her their name. There are thirty-odd people inside already. The party arriving with thirty more and food for sixty changes the building.
scenes.readAloud: “The back alley behind the Library is dark and smells of wet cardboard, and the loading-dock door opens three inches on a chain before you knock. A woman’s face, sixty, cropped grey hair, reading glasses pushed up on her head. ‘Names,’ she says. ‘Every one of you. I’m not letting in anybody whose name I don’t know.’ Behind her, down a corridor lit by emergency lights, you can hear a room full of people being very, very quiet, and a child somewhere asking for its mother, and being hushed.”

skillChecks.success: Peg lets everyone in and puts the party in charge of something — the kitchen, the first-aid room, the door. By midnight she defers to them.
skillChecks.failure: She lets everyone in, but slowly, and the twenty minutes in the alley are a Keep Walking problem of their own.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Peg is the shelter's conscience and the party's ally; she is not a companion NPC but should be memorable. If Hector cooks — on a camp stove in the staff kitchen, quietly, rice and beans and sofrito for sixty — every Group in the building gains +1 Calm and the shelter becomes his. Let that be a big scene.
loot: A shelter: water, toilets, thick walls, and the stacks

scenes.name: Gerry Voss
scenes.description: Gerry Voss, fifty, a building manager from the Middle Wards, has a 9mm pistol he bought legally in another state and carried illegally on this island for six years. He has decided that the Library's doors need guarding with it, and he is standing at the front of the reading room with the gun in his hand, telling people what will happen if 'one of those things' comes in. He has not slept since the phone tone and his hand is shaking.
scenes.readAloud: “He has put a chair in the middle of the reading room, facing the main doors, and he is sitting on it with a pistol on his knee and his finger on the trigger guard, and every time a pipe ticks somewhere in the building his whole body jerks. ‘Nobody opens those doors,’ he says, to nobody. ‘Anything comes through them, I’ll — I’ll handle it.’ He sees you looking. ‘You got a problem?’ He is not a bad man. He is a man who has one idea, and it is a gun.”

skillChecks.success: He is not aggressive. He is terrified, and he needs a job and a reason to put the gun down that is not losing.
skillChecks.failure: A man with a gun who does not like you.

skillChecks.success: You give him a job — the roof watch, the radio, the door — that is more important than the chair, and the gun goes back in his waistband with the safety on. He becomes useful, and later loyal.
skillChecks.failure: He refuses, and stays in the chair, and at 2 A.M. when the Glitter starts playing the concourse screams back into the reading room he stands up with the pistol.

skillChecks.success: Calla (or anyone) gets the magazine out of the pistol while he is asleep at 1 A.M. He does not notice until he needs it. The 9mm pistol has 12 rounds.
skillChecks.failure: He wakes up. Now it is a scene.

skillChecks.success: Lo Pruitt, retired sergeant, takes the gun off him with a voice and a hand. He gives it up, and he hates her for it, and he will be trouble on Day 2.
skillChecks.failure: He points it at you. Nobody in the room breathes. Roll initiative only if someone moves.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the campaign's first statement about guns, and it is a quiet one. A single shot inside the Library is +3 Attention for the building and will bring a Stilt to the front steps by dawn, where it will stand reading the bronze doors for the whole of Day 2 morning. A gunshot does not get anyone killed here; it gets the shelter besieged. If the party ends up with Gerry's pistol, they have their first gun and 12 rounds, and they should feel the weight of it.

scenes.name: 2 A.M.
scenes.description: The power is still on (it fails at noon on Day 2). At 2 A.M. the reading room's high windows fill with a soft drifting shimmer as a Glitter swarm comes in through a broken pane thirty feet up, and the reading room begins to play back, very quietly and then not quietly, the sounds of the Union Terminal concourse at 4:13: the stampede, four hundred people screaming, and individual voices — including, if the GM wishes, a player character's.
scenes.readAloud: “You wake to someone screaming and it takes you a long moment to understand that it is not anybody in the room. The sound is coming from the air — from the high windows, from the coffered ceiling, from everywhere, a whole concourse of panic played back softly and then louder, and in it, quite clearly, a woman’s voice shouting a child’s name, and then a man’s, and then yours. Forty-one people sit up in the dark. Up near the ceiling, in the light from the street, something is glittering, slowly, like dust in a sunbeam, and it is turning toward the sound of the first person who screams.”

skillChecks.skill: Keep Walking (Group: keep the room still)
skillChecks.success: The shelter holds still. The playback runs for four minutes and stops, and the Glitter drifts out of the window it came in by, and the Attention in the building is still 2. Every Group gains +1 Calm from having done it.
skillChecks.failure: Somebody screams back. The Glitter descends on them (Static) and the Attention in the building climbs: at 4, a Stilt walks up Forty-First Street and stands reading the front doors until dawn.

skillChecks.success: June or Haddad (if present) realises what it is: a recording. It is listening, and it is playing back what it heard — as if checking it. That is the first clue that the Visitors are recording the city.
skillChecks.failure: Something in the ceiling is screaming with your voice.

skillChecks.success: Benny, or anyone, does the unthinkable: talks over it, softly and steadily, in a tour-guide voice, telling the room the history of the reading room's ceiling. It is boring, steady, ordinary — and the Glitter ignores the room and follows the playback instead. Advantage on the Group check.
skillChecks.failure: Your voice cracks and that is new.

combatEncounters.tactics: It descends only on creatures that scream, strike it, spray it or burn it. A fire extinguisher (2d6 cold to the swarm) or a burning book will drive it off. Killing it is fine, but makes noise: +1 Attention per round of fighting.
combatEncounters.terrain: A dark reading room thirty feet high, long oak tables, brass lamps, forty-one frightened people on the floor.
combatEncounters.statblock: GLITTER (Medium swarm of Tiny aberrations, CR 1). AC 12. HP 22 (5d8). Speed 0 ft, fly 30 ft (hover). STR 3 (-4) DEX 15 (+2) CON 10 (+0) INT 1 (-5) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 1 (-5). Resistances bludgeoning, piercing, slashing. Immunities grappled, paralyzed, prone, restrained, frightened. Senses blindsight 60 ft. Swarm: it can occupy another creature's space and move through openings an inch wide; it cannot regain HP. Record: the Glitter remembers every sound made within 30 ft of it. It replays them later, elsewhere, at random — a dead man's voice, the party's names, a gunshot — and each replay in a scene is +1 Attention. Harmless in Pattern: a Glitter swarm does not attack anything unless it is struck, sprayed, burned or shouted at from inside it. Actions — Static: every creature in the swarm's space makes a CON save DC 12, 2d6 lightning damage on a failure, half on a success (1d6 if the swarm is at half HP or less). Behaviour: drifts like dust in a sunbeam, towards novelty. It is the Visitors' ears. Fire disperses it (a burning swarm takes double damage), and a fire extinguisher's cone deals it 2d6 cold.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the horror beat of the scenario. Keep it slow. If a player character's voice is in the playback, use something they actually said in Act 1. The scene should leave the table with two things: the Visitors hear everything, and they are keeping it.

scenes.name: Six O'Clock
scenes.description: Dawn. Peg Odinga's hand-crank radio picks up a mainland AM station: an emergency broadcast saying the island is surrounded by 'an unexplained barrier phenomenon', that boats, aircraft and swimmers who approach it are 'returned', that all residents should shelter in place, and that a Joint Task Force has been established. Then, at 6:00 A.M. exactly, three miles away down the empty avenues, the Pier Point ferry blows its horn — two long blasts, the departure signal — exactly on schedule.
scenes.readAloud: “The radio has been hissing for an hour on Peg Odinga’s desk and then it is suddenly a voice, a mainland newsreader’s voice, very calm, reading something she has been given: ‘…an unexplained barrier phenomenon approximately four hundred yards from the shoreline… vessels and aircraft approaching it have been returned… residents should shelter in place…’ Nobody in the reading room moves. And then, from far away to the south, carrying up the empty avenues of a city with no traffic in it, clear as a church bell: two long blasts on a ship’s horn. Walt Kubiak, if he were here, could tell you what that is. It is the Margaret Duane, leaving Pier Point. It is six o’clock. She is on time.”

skillChecks.success: Lo, Benny or Teo knows the horn: the Pier Point ferry's two-blast departure signal. The ferry is running. Who is running it?
skillChecks.failure: A ship's horn, somewhere south.

skillChecks.success: From the roof, through binoculars or a phone zoom, you can see Kestrel Avenue at 6:30: a few people walking north and south, very calmly, coffee in hand, toward the subway entrances that have no trains. Commuters. Some of them are Set. Some of them are not. And the Stilt on the corner is ignoring all of them.
skillChecks.failure: A few figures, far off, walking.

scenes.roleplayNotes: End on the horn. Do not explain it. The next scenario begins with the party deciding where to go, and the ferry is now a question in every player's mind. Award levels: the party reaches level 2 here.

npcsInvolved.name: Calla Moreno, 16
npcsInvolved.description: A graffiti writer who has been mostly not-living at her aunt's in the Steeps for two years and knows the roofs and the Under better than anyone. She set off the car alarm on Forty-Third Street at 4:31 to see what would happen, and a woman was Lifted. She joins the party at the alarm or at the Library. See her companion file.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get to her eight-year-old brother Nico in the Steeps; never get on a boat; never tell anyone about the alarm.

npcsInvolved.name: Margaret 'Peg' Odinga, 60
npcsInvolved.role: Night librarian of the Forty-First Street Library / shelter keeper
npcsInvolved.description: Kenyan-born, unflappable, a reader of everything, who refused to go home because 'somebody has to be here when people come'. She keeps a list of every name in the building and will keep it all week.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep the Library open and the people in it alive. She will stay on the island to the end if anyone is still in the building, and the party may have to talk her out of it in lf-scenario-004.

npcsInvolved.name: Gerry Voss, 50
npcsInvolved.description: Building manager from the Middle Wards with an illegally carried 9mm pistol and one idea. Not a villain; a man whose fear has found an object.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To feel safe. If he is given a job he becomes reliable; if he is humiliated he becomes the shelter's problem in lf-scenario-002.

npcsInvolved.name: Benny's Fourteen
npcsInvolved.description: The Lindqvists (Swedish, sixties), the Okafors and their eight-year-old twins Ada and Obi, the Brennan sisters from Cork, Mr. and Mrs. Tanaka, two backpackers from Leeds called Jas and Rory, a honeymoon couple from Ohio (Kayleigh and Dustin), and Mr. Abraham Feld, eighty-one, travelling alone. Start at Calm 3.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get home. Mr. Feld has come to Merriwick to see the street he was born on, in the Middle Wards, for the last time, and he has a pancreatic cancer diagnosis he has told no one about.

npcsInvolved.name: Marisol Peña, DeShawn Archer and Pilar Wu
npcsInvolved.description: Three AP Chemistry students, sixteen and seventeen. Marisol is in charge; DeShawn is funny and terrified; Pilar is quiet and runs. If the party does not watch her, Pilar runs on Bramwell Avenue in Act 2 and is Lifted — and is waiting, Set, in the Greensward in lf-scenario-002. Start at Calm 2.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get home to their families in Eastgate and Harlow. The other nine students from the trip are scattered across the Meridian and are mostly fine.

npcsInvolved.name: Dee, Kwame and Rafi
npcsInvolved.description: Dee Morales (forty, line cook, sardonic), Kwame Asante (twenty-six, pastry, gentle) and Rafi Duarte (fifteen, dishwasher, films everything). Start at Calm 2.

npcsInvolved.name: Andre Banks, 19
npcsInvolved.description: Getting insulin for his twelve-year-old sister in the Middle Wards. If treated decently he is the first person on the island to walk across town In Pattern on purpose, at dawn on Day 2, having learned it from the party.

rewards.money: $0 to spare — money is still worth something on Day 1, briefly. Wallets left on the concourse and the avenue add up to about $600 if anyone is the kind of person who picks them up; by Day 3 nobody will take cash for anything.
items: Food for about sixty people for two days from Osteria Sette's walk-in (if the party brings it)
Pharmacy medicine: a week of insulin, antibiotics, inhalers and painkillers for forty people (if Abena chooses well)
Batteries (48 AA, 48 AAA), flashlights, a hand-crank phone charger
Gerry Voss's 9mm pistol and 12 rounds (if taken)
A 9mm pistol and 9 rounds from an SUV's glovebox on Forty-Third (if found; its alarm is armed)
Rafi's nine-second video of the woman with the coffee
June's notebook: the first written statement of the In Pattern hypothesis
rewards.story: The party ends Day 1 in the Library with between twenty and sixty people who now depend on them, a hypothesis ('they don't see you if you're boring'), a sky with a Lantern in it, and the ferry horn at six. The xp figure is per character: it takes each from level 1 to level 2.

twists: The Visitors are not hostile. Nobody in this scenario is killed by them; the people they Lift are not dead. The players will assume an invasion. Let them. The truth arrives slowly over four scenarios: the Visitors are keeping the city, and the people they take are being kept.
The most dangerous person in the first night is a frightened man with a pistol, not anything from the sky.
Calla set off the car alarm. The woman in the green raincoat who was Lifted because of it will be found in lf-scenario-002, still filming.
dmTips: OPENING POSITIONS AT 4:12. Lo Pruitt: on the concourse with a coffee, waiting for the 4:30 Green Line. Teo Vasquez-Lind: on his bike on Kestrel Avenue, passing the Terminal, his last drop (the drives for Dr. Haddad) in his bag. Abena Osei-Grant: in the concourse newsagent, buying birthday cards. Hector Salgado: in the kitchen of Osteria Sette, two blocks west on Forty-First. June Halvorsen: on the concourse with twelve students, by the departure board. Benny Szabo: at the wheel of bus #14 at the kerb outside the Terminal, mid-speech. Cut between them fast, then bring them together at the bus — it is big, it is yellow, and it has a PA system.

DO NOT STATE THE RULE. In Pattern is the campaign's central discovery and the players must earn it. Show it: the woman with the coffee, the Set taxi idling through green lights, the cyclist who pedals on and the one who stops. When a player says 'they only take people who run', say nothing, and have the next thing they see confirm it. June Halvorsen's player is the natural person to say it first; Teo's is the natural person to test it.

THE VISITORS DO NOT FIGHT. A Stilt Lifts; it does not hunt. Its Lift damage represents a terrible grip, not intent. If a PC is Lifted, give the party two rounds to get them back (Athletics vs. DC 15 to break the grapple, or enough damage to make it drop them — 15 in one round — at which point the Attention goes to 6) before the PC is carried off. A Lifted PC is not dead: in this scenario the GM should treat it as a cliffhanger and return them in lf-scenario-002, Set, in the Greensward, where the party can wake them. Use this sparingly.

TRACK ATTENTION OPENLY AS MOOD. Players should learn to feel it: 'the Glitter has come down off the ceiling', 'you can hear something stepping between cars two blocks up'. Never give the number, always give the feeling.
THE CIVILIANS ARE THE STAKES. Give the Groups faces. Name the twins. Let Mr. Feld be slow. The party will make better decisions, and harder ones, when they know whose names they are making them for.

GUNS. Lo Pruitt has a .38 and eighteen rounds and has been trained to draw it in danger. Make the players feel what a shot will cost before anyone takes one. When someone does fire — and someone will — let the shot work exactly as the gunplay rules say, then show the Attention spike: a Stilt turning at the end of the street, the Glitter coming down like snow.
LEVEL UP AT DAWN. The party reaches level 2 at the ferry horn. Tell them so; it is a welcome and earned moment.
